title: The reveal
premise: You are walking somewhere and the viewer cannot see where. The location arrives on the drop. The strongest open loop there is.

copy.hook: Nobody told me this place existed

shots.what: Feet on a path, a hand on a door, a bus window — anywhere but the destination
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Camera low, pointed down at your feet, walking. The rule for this whole first half: the viewer must not be able to guess where you are.

shots.what: A closed frame that hides the view — trees, a wall, a corridor, fog
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Find something that physically blocks the horizon and shoot into it. You are buying the payoff here.

shots.what: Moving toward it — walking, climbing, a road ahead
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Walk away from the camera into the frame. Keep the horizon out of shot or high in it.

shots.what: A detail of the place that gives nothing away — a sign, water, a texture
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: A slow deliberate pan across it. Pans give the editor a direction to whip out of; a static detail gives nothing.

shots.what: You, from behind, about to arrive
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Frame so your body blocks most of what is beyond you. This is the last shot before the reveal.

shots.what: The reveal. The widest, most complete view of the place.
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Start pointed at the ground or behind an obstruction and tilt or step out into the view. One continuous move, six seconds, no cuts. Shoot it four times — this single shot is most of the reel.

shots.what: You inside the view, small against it
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Put yourself in the bottom third and let the place fill the rest. Scale is what makes a landscape read on a phone.

shots.what: A calm hold on the place, or you looking out at it
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Hold five seconds, camera still. Leave the centre of the frame clear for the text.
